scope: Theorem 8.1 (Dyadic distribution bound) of the manuscript “Endpoint convergence for the planar Schrodinger equation” (preprints/Endpoint-convergence-for-the-planar-Schrodinger-equation-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 080 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 68d6affc8c3cc3bc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 60. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are fixed p > 2 and σ > 0 with the following property. Let U be a finite sum of the atoms in (2.2), of packet size L ≥ 1, with P α |cα|2 ≤ 1. Suppose that µ is supported in a spatial box of side O(L2) and in |t| ≤ L2, that µ(Br) ≤ mr2 for every ball of radius r ≥ 1, and that (2.4) holds for every label, with 1 ≤ D ≤ L. Then, for every g > 0, µ(A) ≤ CmL4 D−σ g−p , A = {z : |U(z)| ≥ λ}, λ = gL−4/3 . (8.1) The constant is uniform in L, D, g, m and the size of the array. It may depend on the fixed packet class, including sufficiently many finite profile derivative bounds. For an arbitrary coefficient array, the right side is multiplied by ∥c∥p ℓ2 .
